podcast.body: This was Franklin's major label debut album for Columbia Records, recorded with a jazz trio. It was primarily a collection of standards and compositions by proven songwriters, serving as a studio experiment by Columbia to determine the best approach for Aretha's voice, including a cover of "Over the Rainbow" from The Wizard of Oz. "These singles were found on Franklin's major label debut album, simply titled Aretha."

podcast.body: This was Franklin's 31st studio LP and the third time she used "Aritha" as an album title. Its cover was famously painted by pop art legend Andy Warhol, marking the last work he completed before his death in 1987. Narada Michael Walden produced most tracks, with Franklin producing some herself, and Keith Richards contributing to the single "Jumpin' Jack Flash." "In a flex, Arista hired pop art legend Andy Warhol to paint the Aritha album cover. It would be the last work he completed before his 1987 death."
